proof_summary: Take \(n=14\): the condition that \(2k+1\) be prime restricts \(0<k<14\) to \(k=1,2,3,5,6,8,9,11\), for which the adjacent prime-count pairs are respectively \((6,3),(3,4),(4,3),(3,4),(4,2),(4,1),(1,4),(2,3)\). Thus none of these candidates has equal counts, so the required witness does not exist even though \(14>1\) and \(14\ne8\).
